subject: Order form questions — tail claims, IP scope, and boundary points
messages:

Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: RFP questionnaire — legal section (order form + liability)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the final legal questionnaire for order form and liability items — our GC flagged a couple of items we need clarified before moving to signature:

- Tail claims / survivability language for ordered services (we typically require 2 years for indemnity claims post-termination).
- IP scope: confirmation that customer data and custom prompts remain customer property; we need clarity on model improvements derived from customer inputs.
- Liability cap carve-outs for willful misconduct and data breach handling.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on these and return any redlines to the order form? We are targeting a PO + DocuSign by 2026-08-10.

Attachment: Aurelia_RFP_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Emily Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP questionnaire — legal section (order form + liability)

Emily —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Attached is a clean draft of our standard order form and a short one-page summary addressing the three points you called out. High level:

- Tail claims / survivability: Redwood is typically willing to accept survivability of obligations for indemnity claims for 12 months post-termination; we can extend to 24 months for strategic, enterprise agreements subject to volume tiers in the order form. We captured this conditional offer in Section 6 of the attached draft.

- IP scope: Customer data and customer-provided prompts remain the customer’s property. Redwood does not claim ownership of customer prompts or customer data. For model improvements, our standard language grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, aggregated-use right to improve service quality while ensuring that no customer-identifiable data is used to train public models. We included a clarified clause at Exhibit B.

- Liability cap carve-outs: Our standard liability cap is the greater of (i) 12 months of fees paid under the order form or (ii) $1M. We accept carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and violations of data protection law. For breach scenarios involving misappropriation of customer data, we propose the same carve-outs plus mandatory incident response commitments (Section 7).

I've copied Ben here to coordinate commercial terms and next steps. I will loop in Legal (Laura Bennett) for a targeted review and redlines on the order form; expect a short redline within 48 hours. If your GC prefers, we can also provide a marked-up word doc via DocuSign link.

Attachments: RI_OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: RFP questionnaire — legal section (order form + liability)

Sofia / Ben —

Quick legal redline summary after reviewing the draft and the questionnaire:

1) Tail claims (survivability):
- Our baseline is 12 months. For Aurelia, because this is a multi-year strategic deployment, we can agree to 24 months if they commit to the Reserved Capacity tier (see commercial note for Ben).
- Add explicit language that indemnity obligations tied to third-party IP claims are limited to infringement claims directly caused by Redwood software and do not apply to customer content or configuration.

2) IP & model improvements:
- Clarify that any model improvements are applied to aggregated, de-identified telemetry and are not traceable to customer prompts. Add clause to Exhibit B to prohibit using customer-identifying logs for training.
- Add an optional Data Processing Addendum (DPA) reference for PHI/workflows that may require special handling.

3) Liability cap carve-outs:
- We will list carve-outs for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and breach of confidentiality/Data Protection laws.
- For data breaches, define required notification timelines (48 hours initial notification, 7 days for preliminary report) and remediation cooperation commitments.

4) Insurance: specify cyber and E&O limits that match the liability cap negotiation.

I attached the word redline and included inline comments where Aurelia's requested 24-month survivability would require a commercial commitment.

Attachment: RI_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Ben — suggest you surface the revenue/Reserved Capacity ask in the commercial reply. Sofia — once Ben confirms, I'll finalize the redline and prepare an exec summary that the AE can share with Aurelia GC.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
